seo.og_title: Meknes Travel Guide | Medina, Imperial Monuments, Volubilis & Riads | MoroccoTripMap
seo.og_description: Medina, imperial gates, historic granaries, riads and a ready-made itinerary for Meknes, all in one guide.

name: Meknes
hero_subtitle: Bab Mansour, Place el-Hedim, Heri es-Souani and the gateway to Roman Volubilis — Ismail’s imperial capital.

overview.title: Meknes: imperial gates, royal granaries and the road to Volubilis
overview.p1: Meknes is the imposing imperial city of Sultan Moulay Ismail, with massive walls, vast granaries and a medina calmer than Fez. Place el-Hedim and Bab Mansour set the tone; Heri es-Souani shows the scale of royal logistics.
overview.p2: Two full days cover the imperial sights and medina at a relaxed pace; a third day is ideal for Volubilis and the hillside town of Moulay Idriss Zerhoun.

places.title: Must-visit places in Meknes
places.subtitle: Historic gates, royal granaries, Roman ruins and the sites not to miss.

bab.title: Bab Mansour
bab.desc: North Africa’s most famous imperial gate, clad in zellige and monumental detail.

hedim.title: Place el-Hedim
hedim.desc: The beating heart of Meknes — storytellers, musicians and local cafés.

heri.title: Heri es-Souani
heri.desc: Vast royal stables and granaries built to withstand siege and house imperial horses.

volubilis.title: Volubilis
volubilis.desc: UNESCO Roman site with preserved mosaics and triumphal arches.

ismail.title: Mausoleum of Moulay Ismail
ismail.desc: Historic resting place with fine Moroccan decoration and quiet courtyards.

medina.title: Meknes medina & souks
medina.desc: Craft souks and residential lanes with a local, unhurried feel.

medersa.title: Bou Inania Medersa
medersa.desc: 14th-century Quranic school with wood carving and striking zellige.

jamai.title: Dar Jamaï Museum
jamai.desc: Late 19th-century palace displaying Moroccan arts, carpets and objects.

idriss.title: Moulay Idriss Zerhoun
idriss.desc: Historic hillside town stacked above green slopes near Volubilis.

itinerary.title: Suggested 3-day itinerary
itinerary.subtitle: A balanced plan for imperial monuments and Roman ruins.

detailed_itinerary.day1_md: Start on Place el-Hedim and take in Bab Mansour in morning light.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ad: Wander craft souks and residential lanes at an easy pace.
detailed_itinerary.day1_e: Evening — Mint tea on a terrace
detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Relax at a café overlooking the square as evening falls.
detailed_itinerary.day2_md: Explore the royal granaries and stables, then the Mausoleum of Moulay Ismail.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ad: Visit the Bou Inania Medersa and the arts museum at Dar Jamaï.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ed: Enjoy a Moroccan tajine in a riad courtyard.
detailed_itinerary.day3_md: Short trip to Volubilis to walk among Roman columns and mosaics.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ad: Stop in the sacred hillside town for views and local sweets.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ed: A final dinner in town before continuing your journey.

stays.title: Where to stay in Meknes? Our favourites
stays.subtitle: Traditional riads in the medina and comfortable hotels near the main sights.

card1.name: Riad Zerhoun Meknes
card1.desc: Charming riad with warm hospitality and authentic atmosphere in the old city.

card2.name: Ibis Meknes
card2.desc: Practical, comfortable stay close to the train station and main roads.

card3.name: Dar Meknes
card3.desc: Quiet hideaway blending traditional architecture with modern comforts.

card4.name: Riad Bab Berdaine
card4.desc: Traditional house with a lovely rooftop overlooking the historic walls.

booking_banner.title: Explore all places to stay in Meknes
booking_banner.desc: Compare live rates, read traveller reviews and discover more riads and hotels on Booking.com.

eat.title: Where to eat in Meknes
eat.subtitle: Family-friendly Moroccan tables near Place el-Hedim, the medina and the imperial quarter — tajines, couscous and local atmosphere.

omnia.title: Restaurant Omnia
omnia.desc: Reliable traditional kitchen close to the medina — tajines, couscous and a calm family setting.

collier.title: Collier de la Colombe
collier.desc: Rooftop views over the medina and walls — Moroccan classics in a welcoming setting.

yahala.title: Restaurant Ya Hala
yahala.desc: Popular local address for generous portions and classic Meknes home-style cooking.

zitouna.title: Restaurant Zitouna
zitouna.desc: Simple, well-cooked Moroccan dishes in a quiet spot close to the historic ramparts.

bahia.title: Café Restaurant Bahia
bahia.desc: Terrace overlooking Place el-Hedim — ideal for mint tea, snacks and people-watching.

sultana.title: Dar Sultana
sultana.desc: Courtyard or rooftop table in a traditional house — slow Moroccan meals in a peaceful atmosphere.

transport.title: Getting around
transport.desc: The medina and Place el-Hedim are best on foot. Use petit taxis for Heri es-Souani and grand taxis or arranged transport for Volubilis.

bargain.title: Souk bargaining
bargain.desc: Shopping in Meknes is calmer than in Marrakech or Fez; gentle bargaining still applies for crafts.

water.title: Hydration & weather
water.desc: Spring and autumn are ideal for walking the walls and Volubilis. Always carry water.

daytrips.title: Best day trips from Meknes
daytrips.subtitle: Roman history, sacred towns and imperial neighbours within easy reach.

volubilis.title: Volubilis & Moulay Idriss
volubilis.desc: The classic pair of Roman mosaics and the sacred hillside town.

fes.title: Fez imperial city
fes.desc: Only 30–45 minutes by train for a full day in Morocco’s spiritual capital.

atlas.title: Middle Atlas & Ifrane
atlas.desc: Alpine-style town, cedar forests and wild monkeys around Azrou.

q1.question: How many days should I spend in Meknes?
q1.answer: 2 to 3 days is ideal for the imperial monuments, medina and a half-day trip to Volubilis.

q2.question: Is Meknes safe for tourists?
q2.answer: Yes. Meknes is very safe and calmer than Morocco’s larger tourist hubs.

q3.question: What currency is used and can I pay by card?
q3.answer: Morocco uses the dirham (MAD). Cards work in major hotels and restaurants; cash is needed for small shops and taxis.

q4.question: How do I get to Meknes?
q4.answer: Meknes is well linked by ONCF trains from Fez, Rabat, Casablanca and Tangier.
